b: The New Zealand timber manufacturer has partnered with California-based Weaverbird to expand access to its products among architects, designers and builders.
Abodo timber products will be available through Weaverbird in Southern California (Image: Abodo)

New Zealand timber manufacturer Abodo has partnered with Weaverbird Wood Co, a building materials and lumber supplier based in Southern California, to make its products available to the region’s architecture and design sector.

The partnership adds Abodo to Weaverbird’s portfolio of natural wood products, giving local architects, designers and builders access to its timber range through the supplier’s showroom in Corona del Mar and mill in Ontario.

Weaverbird provides project support through its Design to Delivery approach, which covers material selection, estimating, customisation and delivery planning. The company works with clients to identify materials that meet each project’s aesthetic, performance, budget and availability requirements.

As part of Abodo’s North American architectural partner network, Weaverbird will provide guidance on product profiles, finishes and custom millwork options to help clients identify suitable timber solutions for their projects.

“Weaverbird begins with the architect’s vision and works through every material decision needed to bring it to life. That consultative, project-led approach is exactly how we want designers to experience Abodo,” said India Thorp, general manager of growth and brand at Abodo.
Tim Hummel of Weaverbird said the partnership would help the company offer clients timber products that prioritise durability, performance and sustainability.

“Although our roots in the lumber industry run deep, we launched Weaverbird with a forward-looking vision, thinking five, 10, even 15 years ahead, and aligning ourselves with truly sustainable innovations like Abodo,” he said.
